steps.title: Prepare all required solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions exactly as described, noting concentrations, volumes, storage conditions and that the TLC eluent must be used fresh:

substeps.instruction: Ascorbic acid solution (50 mg L⁻¹): dissolve 600 mg L‑ascorbic acid in 12 mL deionized water; use immediately.
Extraction solution: mix 2 mL chloroform, 4.4 mL methanol and 2 mL water; store sealed at room temperature.
Molybdate solution (12 mg L⁻¹): dissolve 144 mg ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate in 12 mL deionized water; use immediately.
Phosphate standard solution (4 mM): dissolve 35.598 mg disodium hydrogen phosphate dihydrate in 50 mL deionized water; store at –20 °C.
Primuline staining solution (0.05 % w/v): dissolve 50 mg primuline in 100 mL water/acetone (20:80 v/v); use immediately.
Reaction solvent: mix 6 mL dichloromethane (DCM) with 1 mL dimethylformamide (DMF); store sealed at room temperature.
TLC eluent (single‑use): combine 30 mL chloroform, 35 mL ethanol, 35 mL triethylamine and 7 mL deionized water directly in the TLC chamber; do not store.

steps.title: Prepare lipid stock solutions
steps.instruction: Handle all lipids in glassware on ice, evaporate solvent under controlled vacuum, and store aliquots at –20 °C:

substeps.instruction: Transfer 10 mg of each lipid from the sealed glass ampoule into a glass screw‑neck vial.
Evaporate chloroform in a glass desiccator at 250 mbar for 3 h, then at 30 mbar for 1 h (final vacuum 10 ± 2 mbar, suction 1.5 m³ h⁻¹).
Cap the vials and store at –20 °C.
When needed, place the vial on ice and dissolve the lipid to 10 mg mL⁻¹ in chloroform (adjust with chloroform/methanol/water if solubility is limited).

steps.title: Set up coupling reaction
steps.instruction: Couple DOPE (or other lipid) with pHrodo Red NHS‑ester (or alternative fluorophore) in glass under nitrogen:

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1–2 mg lipid (based on 500 µg fluorophore) from the chloroform stock into a 10 mL round‑bottom glass tube with NS 14 joint.
Evaporate the chloroform under a gentle N₂ stream at room temperature until dry.
Add a small magnetic stir bar.
Dissolve 500 µg fluorophore in 100 µL reaction solvent (DCM/DMF 6:1) and add to the tube.
Add DIPEA to a final concentration of 130 mM (2.3 µL DIPEA for 100 µL solvent).
Seal with a glass plug, wrap in aluminium foil, place on a magnetic stirrer and stir overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Extract labelled lipid
steps.instruction: Perform a liquid‑liquid extraction to isolate the organic phase containing the labelled lipid:

substeps.instruction: Add sequentially to the reaction mixture: 0.5 mL chloroform, 1 mL methanol, 0.5 mL water, then 0.5 mL chloroform and 0.5 mL water.
Mix gently; the mixture becomes biphasic.
Transfer the coloured bottom (organic) phase to a new glass tube.
If short‑chain lipids are used, repeat chloroform washes until the aqueous phase is colourless.
Dry the collected organic phase by a gentle N₂ stream or a rotary evaporator, depending on volume.

steps.title: Determine Rf by test TLC
steps.instruction: Run a small TLC to locate the product and measure its retention factor:

substeps.instruction: Cut a 5 cm wide silica‑gel TLC plate with a glass cutter and draw a pencil line 1 cm above the bottom.
Spot a few µL of the dissolved lipid stock and of the crude reaction product onto the line using a glass Pasteur pipette; let dry completely.
Fill a TLC chamber with the TLC eluent to a depth of ~0.8 cm and saturate for ~5 min.
Place the plate upright in the chamber, close the lid, and develop until the solvent front is ~1 cm from the top.
Mark the solvent front, dry the plate for ~1 h in the fume hood, then image under white light and long‑wave UV.
Spray the plate with primuline staining solution, let dry, and re‑image under UV.
Calculate Rf = distance of product / distance of mobile phase (expected Rf ≈0.70 for pHrodo‑Red‑DOPE, 0.55 for pHrodo‑Green‑DOPE).

steps.title: Purify product by preparative TLC
steps.instruction: Separate the labelled lipid on a larger TLC plate:

substeps.instruction: Use a 20 cm long silica‑gel TLC plate; draw a line 1 cm above the bottom.
Dissolve the crude product in 100 µL chloroform : methanol (2 : 1, v/v).
Apply the entire solution evenly along the line with a glass Pasteur pipette; dry for ~1 h in the fume hood.
Fill the TLC chamber with the same eluent to ~0.8 cm depth and saturate for 20 min.
Develop the plate upright until the solvent front is ~1 cm below the top.
Dry the plate, image under white light and UV to locate the product band.

steps.title: Re‑extract product from silica
steps.instruction: Recover the labelled lipid from the silica band scraped off the preparative TLC:

substeps.instruction: Scrape the product band into a pointed‑bottom glass tube (no joint).
Add 1 mL extraction solution, vortex 1 min, then centrifuge at 480 × g for 10 min at 8 °C.
Transfer the liquid phase to a fresh glass tube; repeat extraction until the liquid becomes colourless.
Add an equal volume (1:1 v/v) of chloroform and water to induce phase separation.
Transfer the coloured bottom (organic) phase to a new glass tube and dry by N₂ stream or in a desiccator.
Proceed to quantification or store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Optional column chromatography purification
steps.instruction: Further purify the labelled lipid using CM‑Sepharose column chromatography:

substeps.instruction: Assemble a 200 × 10 mm column, place a glass‑wool plug at the bottom, and add 20–25 mL CM‑Sepharose suspension to give a 10 cm stationary phase (1 cm diameter).
Run out excess methanol, tap gently to remove air bubbles, and cover the resin with a 1–3 mm layer of glass beads.
Rinse the column with MeOH/CHCl₃ mixtures according to Table 2 (e.g., 7 mL MeOH + 3 mL CHCl₃, then 5 mL MeOH + 5 mL CHCl₃, etc.).
Dissolve the dried product in ~250 µL chloroform and load onto the column by slowly adding in a circular motion along the wall.
Wash the sample tube with small volumes of solvent until colourless, then apply to the column.
Elute with a gradient of increasing MeOH content in CHCl₃ as listed in Table 3, collecting 10 mL fractions in glass tubes.
Evaporate each fraction (desiccator or rotary evaporator) and identify product‑containing fractions by TLC.
Combine product fractions, dry, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify phosphate content (Bartlett assay)
steps.instruction: Determine the amount of lipid‑bound phosphate using a colorimetric assay:

substeps.instruction: Turn on an electrical heating block in the fume hood and set to 195 °C.
Prepare triplicate sample tubes: dissolve the purified lipid in enough chloroform and transfer ~20 nmol (assuming 100 % yield) to each glass tube; evaporate solvent with N₂.
Prepare phosphate standards: dilute the 0.4 mM phosphate standard to obtain 0, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 nmol phosphate (add 0, 12.5, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125 µL respectively to separate tubes).
Add 650 µL perchloric acid to every tube (samples and standards) and loosely cover with glass marbles.
Heat all tubes at 195 °C for 1–2 h until solutions become clear; cool to room temperature.
Place a water bath at 80 °C. Add 3.3 mL deionized water to each tube, vortex.
Add 0.5 mL molybdate solution, vortex; then add 0.5 mL ascorbic acid solution, vortex.
Boil the tubes at 80 °C for 10 min, then cool to room temperature.
Transfer each sample (in duplicate) to a 96‑well plate.
Measure absorbance at 812 nm (optional 780 nm or 720 nm) with a microplate reader.

Average duplicate readings, subtract the blank (0 nmol) value, plot absorbance vs. phosphate amount, perform linear regression (y = mx, b ≈ 0), and calculate sample phosphate concentration from the regression line.
Convert phosphate amount to lipid concentration as needed.

steps.title: Analyze product (optional)
steps.instruction: Confirm the molecular weight of the labelled lipid by mass spectrometry (e.g., MALDI‑TOF) as described in the original protocol.
